title: Eventual separatedness over a fixed quasi-separated algebraic-space base
statement: Work over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ with schemes [def-pc-scheme] and algebraic spaces [def-trf-algebraic-space] in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Fibre products are sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. A space is quasi-compact if it admits a surjective etale atlas from a quasi-compact scheme. A morphism is quasi-compact if its pullback to every affine scheme has quasi-compact source; quasi-separated means that its diagonal is quasi-compact, and a space is quasi-separated when its absolute diagonal is quasi-compact. A closed immersion is representable and is a closed immersion on each scheme test [def-weil-closed-immersion]; separated means that the relative diagonal is a closed immersion. A morphism is affine if its pullback to every affine scheme is an affine scheme. Let $Y$ be a quasi-separated algebraic space, let $I$ be a small nonempty directed partially ordered set, and let $(X_a\to Y)_{a\in I}$ be an inverse system of quasi-compact quasi-separated algebraic spaces with affine transition morphisms $X_b\to X_a$ for $a\le b$. Let a cone $X\to X_a$ exhibit $X=\varprojlim_a X_a$ in algebraic spaces over $Y$. If $X\to Y$ is separated, there exists $a_0\in I$ such that $X_a\to Y$ is separated for every $a\ge a_0$. No finite-presentation hypothesis on the stage morphisms and no quasi-compactness hypothesis on $Y$ are imposed.

proof.text: Choose $o\in I$ and an affine surjective etale atlas $U_o\to X_o$ by [lem-trf-space-qc-finite-affine-atlas-refinement]. Apply [lem-sfb-space-fixed-base-atlas-relation-tower] to $(X_a\to Y)$. Retain its notation $U_a,U,R_a,R,s_a,t_a,s,t,j_a,u_{ba}$. In particular all mixed products used below are quasi-compact separated schemes, the relation projections are of finite type, and the atlas tower has limit $U$. This uses quasi-separatedness of $Y$, not quasi-compactness or finite presentation over $Y$.

source.place: Tag 086X (lemma-eventually-separated), reduction to Tag 084T (lemma-descend-separated); Tag 084T first paragraph, applied directly to relative mixed products over Y.

proof.text:
The map $j=(s,t):R\to U\times_YU$ is the scheme test of the closed relative diagonal of $X\to Y$, so is a closed immersion. Indeed on every test scheme the pullback of the diagonal consists of pairs of atlas sections with equal image in $X$, precisely the sections of $R$; these identifications commute with restriction and preserve both projections. Fix the index $o$ and consider $V_a=U_a\times_YU$ over the scheme $U$ by its second projection. The helper gives affine transitions, quasi-compact stages and limit $U\times_YU$ (use its arbitrary affine $W$ clause with $W=U$, and interchange factors). Since $R\to U$ is of finite type, [pqf-lem-limit-immersion-descends] applied to $j$ gives $a\ge o$ such that
$$h_{a,\infty}:R\longrightarrow U_a\times_YU,\qquad r\longmapsto(u_a s(r),t(r))$$
is a closed immersion. Here $u_a:U\to U_a$ is the limit projection.

source.place: Tag 084T (lemma-descend-separated), sentence applying limits.tex Tag 081B (lemma-finite-type-eventually-closed), clause (1), with relative products over Y.

proof.text: Fix this $a$. Over the affine scheme $U_a$ using the second coordinate, take the tower $U_b$ for $b\ge a$ with limit $U$. The helper identifies the morphisms $h_{a,b}:R_b\to U_a\times_YU_b$ with the base changes of $j_a:R_a\to U_a\times_YU_a$ along $U_b\to U_a$, and its limit base change with $h_{a,\infty}$. The schemes $U_a$, $R_a$, and $U_a\times_YU_a$ are quasi-compact and quasi-separated; $j_a$ is locally of finite type. Thus every hypothesis of [lem-weil-pbc-descend-closed-immersion] holds. Obtain $b\ge a$ such that $h_{a,b}$ is a closed immersion.

Let $q:U_b\times_YU_b\to U_a\times_YU_b$ be $(u_{ba},1)$. It is affine by base change of the affine morphism $u_{ba}$ [lem-sfb-space-affine-locality], and consequently separated as a scheme morphism [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence]. Since $q\circ j_b=h_{a,b}$ is a closed immersion, [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-from-composite] gives that $j_b:R_b\to U_b\times_YU_b$ is a closed immersion.

source.place: Tag 084T (lemma-descend-separated), final sentence; separated cancellation for closed immersions spells out the inference.

proof.text: The scheme map $U_b\times_YU_b\to X_b\times_YX_b$ is surjective etale: factor it as the base change of the atlas on the first factor followed by its base change on the second factor, using [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Representable etale maps are tested on schemes [def-trf-algebraic-space], and composition is etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation]. The pullback of $\Delta_{X_b/Y}$ by this atlas is $j_b$: both sheaves on a test scheme consist of pairs of atlas sections with equal image in $X_b$. Apply [lem-sfb-space-closed-immersion-atlas-locality] to this diagonal to conclude that it is a closed immersion. Hence $X_b\to Y$ is separated.

source.place: Tags 084T and 086X, descent of the closed diagonal from an etale scheme cover; spaces-morphisms.tex Tag 03M4 (lemma-closed-immersion-local).

proof.text: For every $c\ge b$, the affine transition $X_c\to X_b$ is separated by [lem-sfb-space-affine-locality]. Compose it with the separated morphism $X_b\to Y$ using [lem-sfb-space-separated-fp-composition]. Thus $X_c\to Y$ is separated for all $c\ge b$, and $a_0=b$ has the required property.

source.place: Tag 086X (lemma-eventually-separated), all sufficiently large stages; spaces-morphisms.tex Tags 03KQ (lemma-composition-separated) and 03WH (lemma-composition-affine).

The statement and stmt_deps equal those on live and side-live, where the item is still unsplit with no repair note, so this is not superseded. Steps checked: (1) atlas refinement gives an affine atlas because X_o is qc. (2) j is the pullback of Δ_{X/Y}, so it is closed; 081B(1) applies over base U with stages U_a×_Y U (qc, affine transitions, limit U×_Y U) and t of finite type. (3) 01ZP applies over (U_b)_{b≥a}, S_0=U_a: R_b ≅ R_a×_{t_a,U_a}U_b and (U_a×_Y U_a)×_{U_a}U_b = U_a×_Y U_b, so f_b = h_{a,b} and f = h_{a,∞}; j_a is lft. (4) q = u_{ba}×1 is affine, hence separated, and q∘j_b = h_{a,b}, so closed-from-composite applies. (5) U_b×_Y U_b → X_b×_Y X_b is surjective étale as two base changes of the atlas; the pullback of the diagonal is j_b; atlas locality gives a closed diagonal. (6) Affine implies separated, and separated morphisms compose. The new helper lem-sfb-space-fixed-base-atlas-relation-tower is true: mixed products are schemes, qc and separated, via the representable qc Δ_Y into an affine product, and the isomorphisms hold on sections. I tested it on Z_o empty, a constant tower, Y = Spec Z, a non-qc Y and a nonseparated Z_a. It is self-contained and statement-only; it does not restate the item, since all descent work stays in the item's steps. It duplicates none of 0851, 01ZQ, 0850, 07SF or 03HK (no 084T node exists). The h_{a,∞} identification is one line from the helper's limit isomorphism that 'preserves the displayed maps', so no fix was needed. Advisory only: 'separated scheme' carries no citation.
